_comment: The style's colours, the one place to change them (scripts/palette.py). The style guide's prompt blocks name
colours only as {role} (the name below), {role.cap} (capitalised) and {role.hex}; stitch.py draws the board's
flow arrows in the roles under arrows with those weights. name is the colour as the image model reads it (ink
is used as 'pure-<name>', so keep it one word). Every colour must be darker than module.json ink_threshold
(luminance). The board is always white. After a change: render_scenes.py sync (new scene prompts), title.py
build, characters.py build --force, and stitch.py board (Gate 2 again); a board built with other arrow

ink.name: black
ink._use: line work; about 80% of the lettering

main.name: orange-red
main._use: main accent, about two-thirds of the coloured ink: emphasis words, arrows, key highlights

second.name: teal
second._use: second accent, about one-third of the coloured ink: secondary objects and light shading

_arrows: board flow arrows: each arrow's colour is picked with these weights (seeded per arrow; normalised to sum 1). Same split as rsa_animate (the house split stitch.py used for every style before palettes)
